🚀 Product / CS Ops
Go-Live · Functionality Update

California Alternative Workweek 4x10 Settings — Live in Production

CA locations can now enable a 4-days / 10-hour schedule setting per employee so daily overtime starts after 10 hours for approved alternative workweek employees.

CA 4x10 schedule setting available in employee Access & Wages
✅
What sales needs to know: CA customers with an approved 4x10 alternative workweek can now enable “Team member works 4 days, 10-hour shifts, per week” on an employee’s job in Team → Employee Profile → Job Details → Access & Wages.
⚖️
Why it’s changing: CA employers on an approved 4x10 schedule need daily OT to start at 10 hours instead of 8. Homebase already supported this for Nevada; this release extends support to California.
💬
How it impacts day-to-day: If a CA customer asks about 4x10 OT, point them to the employee’s Access & Wages settings. Do not position this as automatic — the customer must opt in per employee after completing California’s alternative workweek election.
📌
Rules that did not change: CA double OT at 12+ hours and 7th-day OT are unchanged. NV-specific behavior is unchanged and does not apply to CA.
Source note: The release is live in production with payroll_california_alternative_workweek enabled 100%. No outbound customer comms are planned.
Rollout · 100%

New Left Navigation — Moving to 100% of Customers June 17

The new web navigation is no longer just a partial rollout. It moves to all customers on Wednesday, June 17.

🧭
What sales needs to know: The new left-hand navigation is rolling out to 100% of customers on Wednesday, June 17.
🔁
Why it’s changing: This is the next phase after the initial rollout. The redesigned navigation becomes the default customer experience.
💬
How it impacts day-to-day: Stop framing this as a limited new-account experiment after June 17. If customers ask where something moved, position it as the same product paths in a cleaner layout.
Rep reminder: Use simple language: “The layout changed, but the core destinations are the same.” Avoid proactively over-explaining unless a customer asks.
📊 RevOps
Live · Blitz Relaunch

Blitz Mode Relaunched Monday with GTM OS Fixes Live

Blitz Mode relaunched Monday, June 15 after a batch of GTM OS fixes went live for account loading, prioritization, cadence behavior, talk tracks, notes, location lists, payroll status, and skip reasons.

⚡
What sales needs to know: Blitz Mode is back in production. The major fixes are live and were verified in staging before launch.
🛠️
Why it’s changing: Rep-reported bugs were slowing the motion down or sending reps to the wrong accounts. The relaunch fixes the biggest blockers before pushing full-time usage.
🎯
How it impacts day-to-day: Reps should see faster account loading, stronger account prioritization by expected revenue, no back-to-back repeat accounts, cleaner talk tracks, accurate note authorship, refreshed payroll status, and a lower minimum for skip/disqualify reasons.
🚩
Watch item: A small task-creation issue was caught live after launch; only two opps were impacted and the fix was already in review. Keep reporting anomalies quickly.
Manager note: Treat this as a production relaunch, not a new motion. The ask is consistent execution plus fast bug reporting if anything feels off.
Live · Inception Team

Inbound Inception Pipeline Is Now in GTM OS

Inbound Inception’s existing pipeline moved into GTM OS on Monday, June 15 with staged cadence placement so reps start from the right step instead of restarting every deal from zero.

1
Connect / Consult / Closing
Existing deals start at Step 1 so reps own the first live touch.
2
New deals · 0 days in stage
Start at Step 1.
3
New deals · 1–2 business days in stage
Start at Step 6.
4
New deals · 3–7 business days in stage
Start at Step 9.
5
New deals · 8+ business days in stage
Start at Step 12 to preserve cadence runway.
📥
What sales needs to know: Inception’s pipeline is live in GTM OS with stage-aware enrollment, not a one-size-fits-all restart.
🧠
Why it’s changing: The team wanted a controlled launch that avoids auto-blasting quiet pipeline and keeps enough cadence runway for aged deals.
☎️
How it impacts day-to-day: Every deal starts on a manual rep-call step first. Automated email and SMS steps resume only as the cadence moves forward.
📧
Action required: Inception reps need to accept the org-wide email setup so automated cadence emails can send from their address. Switchers already have this done.
Operating principle: Reps get a manageable live-call queue on day one, while older deals still have room to work before any auto-close timing catches up.
